result.currentBehavior:
The harness has NO concurrency at any level — it is a strictly serial, single-threaded turn loop, which is neither "barrier" nor "pipeline"; it is "one thing at a time." There are zero concurrency primitives in src/ (no Promise.all/race/allSettled, no worker pool, no in-flight counter; grep over src returns nothing). Three nested serialization points:

(1) TOP-LEVEL RUN LOOP (scripts/run-live-agent-demo.mjs:229 `for (let turn = 1; turn <= maxTurns; turn += 1)`): a single sequential turn counter. Each turn does at most ONE action and almost always `continue`s to the next turn: it observes state, then either handles one fault, or verifies the ONE slice returned by `before.slices.find(isReadyForDeterministicVerify)` (line 332 — find, not filter, so one slice per turn), or runs ONE overseer turn (line 413). Slices are advanced strictly one-at-a-time, one stage per turn; there is no pipelining of distinct slices through distinct stages simultaneously.

(2) OVERSEER COMMAND LOOP (src/cli.ts:5877 `for (let index = 0; index < commands.length; index += 1)`): the bounded commands an overseer recommends (capped by executeLimit, default 3) run in a sequential for-loop, each via a BLOCKING `spawnSync(process.execPath, [process.argv[1], ...cliArgs])` (line 5941). A child-agent dispatch (a nested `swarm run`/`swarm review`) therefore blocks the parent overseer process until that worker/reviewer fully completes before the next command is even started.

(3) PER-SLICE CHILD AGENT (src/cli.ts:2828 spawnWorkerStreaming returns a single awaited Promise resolved on child `close`): exactly one child process is in flight per executeWorkerRun/executeReviewRun call, and the caller awaits it. There is also an EXPLICIT guard (src/cli.ts:6204-6218) that REFUSES to dispatch a child agent if any worker/reviewer run for that slice is already `running` — so worker→review→verify for a single slice is contractually sequential (this is a correct evidence-ordering invariant, not a perf bug).

The planner (src/planner.ts:45 pullNextSlice) is invoked one slice at a time via the `swarm slices pull` CLI command (cli.ts:743) or by the overseer recommending it; it does not batch-create or schedule multiple slices for parallel work. `firstActiveLaneForTarget` (planner.ts:133, storage.ts:328 `... limit 1`) reuses a single active lane by default, so the default planning path funnels everything through one lane. The protocol declares `lanes.maxActiveLanes: 3` (protocol.ts:53, protocol.yaml:12) but this value is NEVER read or enforced anywhere in src (grep for `maxActiveLanes` hits only protocol.ts default, docs, never planner/storage/cli) — there is no lane-level WIP/concurrency control in code at all; it is dead config.

result.workflowComparison: Workflow mechanism 4 (pipeline-no-barrier) says each item flows through ALL stages independently, so wall-clock equals the slowest single chain, not the sum of stage maxes; verifiers can run while a slow reviewer is still working on a different item. agent-swarm is the opposite extreme of even a barrier model: it has neither pipelining NOR fan-out batching. It does not "wait for all workers then review" (barrier) — it never has more than one worker at a time to wait for. Wall-clock = SUM over every slice of (worker + review + verify), fully serialized, plus an extra overseer LLM turn between most stages (the loop almost always does one action then `continue`s, re-invoking the overseer to decide the next single action). Compared to Workflow's content-addressed journal + pipeline that lets N items progress through M stages concurrently with wall-clock ≈ slowest chain, agent-swarm's wall-clock for K slices is roughly K × (overseer-turn + stage latencies) summed. The mission's parallel ambition ("coordinate autonomous implementation agents AT SCALE", lanes as parallel work streams) is structurally unrealized: lanes exist as a data/ownership concept but carry no execution concurrency. The one place agent-swarm is correctly stricter than a naive pipeline is the per-slice worker→review→verify ordering and the "no dispatch while running" guard (cli.ts:6204) — those preserve the evidence-ordering and "workers may not approve their own verification" invariants and must be retained under any parallelization.

gaps.title: No cross-slice/cross-lane concurrency: wall-clock is sum-of-everything
gaps.detail: The top-level loop (run-live-agent-demo.mjs:229) advances one slice, one stage, per turn, and the overseer command loop (cli.ts:5877) executes child agents via blocking spawnSync. K independent slices that share no dependency still run fully serialized, with an overseer LLM turn interleaved between actions. This is the single largest wall-clock cost and directly contradicts the at-scale coordination mission.

gaps.title: maxActiveLanes is dead config — no lane-level concurrency control exists
gaps.detail: protocol.ts:53 and protocol.yaml:12 declare lanes.maxActiveLanes:3, and docs/architecture/protocol-config.md documents per-lane overrides, but grep shows the value is never read in planner.ts, storage.ts, or cli.ts. There is no WIP cap, no per-lane parallelism budget, and no enforcement — so the config implies a scheduling capability the code does not have. A reader/operator would reasonably assume up to 3 lanes run concurrently; none do.

gaps.title: Pipeline barrier baked into the loop shape: one verify per turn
gaps.detail: Even within a single slice's lifecycle, readyForVerify is chosen with Array.find (run-live-agent-demo.mjs:332), so if multiple slices are simultaneously ready_for_review/implemented, only one is verified per turn and the rest wait — a serialization barrier where independent verifications could proceed.

gaps.title: Overseer is a global serialization point and per-turn cost multiplier
gaps.detail: Because nearly every loop branch does one action then continue (e.g. run-live-agent-demo.mjs:264,270,276,282,308,399), an overseer LLM turn (executeOverseerRun, cli.ts:1974, a full driver invocation) is paid between most state transitions. With everything serial, the overseer's own latency is added once per advanced step rather than amortized across parallel progress.

recommendations.title: Pipeline independent slices through stages with a bounded concurrency budget
recommendations.change: Replace the single per-turn action in the run loop (run-live-agent-demo.mjs:229-467) with a scheduler that, each tick, computes the set of slices whose next stage is runnable (dependency-satisfied) and dispatches up to a configured concurrency budget of them via Promise.allSettled over async executeWorkerRun/executeReviewRun (cli.ts:2253/2502, which are already async and return per-run results). Keep verify per-slice (cli.ts verify command) gated behind that slice's own review evidence. Stages advance independently per slice (worker for slice B can run while reviewer for slice A runs), matching Workflow mechanism 4, while the existing 'no dispatch while a run is active for THIS slice' guard (cli.ts:6204) keeps each slice's chain ordered.
recommendations.rationale: Turns wall-clock from sum-over-slices into ~slowest-single-chain for independent work, the core perf win of pipeline-no-barrier, without weakening any per-slice ordering.
recommendations.missionTieIn: Directly realizes 'coordinate autonomous implementation agents at scale' and makes lanes real parallel work streams; status still rolls up from the ledger, not from scheduling.

recommendations.change: Change readyForVerify selection from Array.find (run-live-agent-demo.mjs:332) to filter, and verify every independently-ready slice in the tick (each still independently gated on its own reviewGate/workerGate inside the verify command, cli.ts:973-1002). recommendations.change: Let the deterministic scheduler (SC-1/SC-3) advance unambiguous, dependency-satisfied transitions (dispatch next stage, run ready verifications, clear resolved repair escalations) WITHOUT an intervening executeOverseerRun, and reserve overseer turns (cli.ts:1974) for genuinely ambiguous decisions (blocked work, lane planning, human_required). This mirrors Workflow mechanism 1: deterministic control plane in code, LLM only fills the hard leaves.
recommendations.rationale: The overseer is currently a per-step latency/cost multiplier because the loop does one action then continue; most of those actions are mechanical and need no LLM judgement.
recommendations.missionTieIn: Keeps planner/overseer decisions visible as events for the cases that need judgement, while the deterministic control plane stays replayable and cheap — aligned with the forensic Workflow model and the 'no busy work' maxim.

result.currentBehavior:
A worker/reviewer/overseer result reaches validated harness state via PARSE-THEN-VALIDATE of a driver-written artifact, NOT a forced structured-output tool call enforced at the tool layer. The contract differs per driver, and there is NO harness-level self-retry on malformed output.

Two distinct extraction paths exist:

(1) codex driver (src/worker-driver.ts:60-112): the harness passes `--output-schema <schemaPath> --output-last-message <resultPath>` (lines 79, 97) and lets the codex CLI write the final message to a file. `finalize()` (101-111) then calls `validateResultArtifact()` (116-139): it `fs.existsSync` the file, `JSON.parse`es it (122), and `schema.safeParse`es it (133) against `spec.resultSchema ?? workerResultSchema`. So validation is purely on a file the child process produced; the schema is advisory to codex, enforced only post-hoc by the harness.

(2) claude driver (src/worker-driver.ts:169-252): the harness passes `--json-schema <schemaJson>` and reads `--output-format stream-json`. `finalize()` (219-251) scans stdout backwards via `lastResultEvent()` (147-164) for the `type:"result"` event, reads `resultEvent.structured_output`, `safeParse`es it (225), and on success WRITES it to `spec.resultPath` itself (227). So claude's path does consult a model-emitted `structured_output` field, but the harness still validates after the fact and is responsible for persisting the artifact.

(3) fixture driver: bypasses all of this — `runFixtureWorker` returns a typed object in-process and the CLI does `fs.writeFileSync(lastMessagePath, JSON.stringify(workerResult))` then hardcodes `finalization = { ok: true, structuredResultWritten: true }` (src/cli.ts:2360-2366; review 2607-2618; overseer 2079-2086). No validation at all on the fixture path.

The artifact is then validated a SECOND time when consumed: `readReviewResultFile` (cli.ts:3846-3865), `readOverseerDecisionFile` (5667-5686), and the worker-result verifier (4326-4345) each independently `JSON.parse` + `schema.safeParse` the same file. The JSON Schema handed to drivers is HAND-WRITTEN separately from the Zod schema in `writeWorkerResultSchema`/`writeReviewResultSchema`/`writeOverseerDecisionSchema` (cli.ts:6460-6611) — two parallel definitions of the same contract that can drift.

On malformed output the behavior is BLOCK, never retry: worker `finalize.ok=false` -> slice status "blocked" (cli.ts:2464); review parse failure -> slice "blocked", dependencies blocked, blocker escalation inserted (2740-2744); overseer parse failure -> `overseer.failed` event + blocked heartbeat (2183-2219). Recovery from a malformed result is operator-driven (recovery revive/restart commands), not an automatic same-call re-ask. There is one silent-success edge: codex `finalize` returns `ok` based ONLY on artifact validity and treats a non-zero exit code as a recoverable success (`resultArtifactRecoveryReason`, worker-driver.ts:141-145) — a valid file overrides a crashed process.
result.workflowComparison: Workflow mechanism 3 (schema-enforced output) forces a StructuredOutput tool call and validates AT THE TOOL LAYER, so the model SELF-RETRIES inside the same agent() call until the object is valid — the caller receives a typed object and never parses prose (one agent retried 7x). Agent-swarm inverts this: validation happens OUTSIDE the model turn, after the child process exits, against a file or a stdout-scraped field. The model is told the schema (codex `--output-schema`, claude `--json-schema`) but nothing forces a conformant emission; a malformed/missing artifact ends the turn and the harness blocks. There is no in-turn retry loop anywhere in src/ (grep for retry/self-retry/attempt < found only operator-driven restart/revive and overseer coaching). The fixture path matches Workflow's "typed object, never parse" ideal by construction, but only because it never crosses a process boundary. Net: agent-swarm gets schema-typed RESULTS (good — Zod is the gate at two points) but pays for it with brittleness Workflow designed away: per-driver extraction divergence, a hand-maintained second schema, and block-instead-of-self-heal on the most common failure (model emitted near-miss JSON).

gaps.title: No self-retry on malformed structured output; a single near-miss blocks the slice
gaps.detail: When a real driver emits invalid/absent structured output, finalize fails and the slice/dependencies go to 'blocked' with an escalation (cli.ts:2464, 2740-2744, 2183-2219). Workflow mechanism 3 would have the model self-correct in-turn. Today the cheapest, most common failure (model produced 90%-correct JSON) costs a full operator-driven revive/restart cycle and stalls dependents — directly taxing verified-state throughput and creating drift between 'work happened' and 'work captured'.

gaps.title: Hand-written JSON Schema is a second source of truth that can silently drift from Zod
gaps.detail: writeWorkerResultSchema/writeReviewResultSchema/writeOverseerDecisionSchema (cli.ts:6460-6611) duplicate schemas.ts by hand. Drift is asymmetric and dangerous: if the JSON Schema is looser/wronger than Zod, the driver is guided toward output Zod will reject (-> avoidable blocks); if it omits a field Zod made optional via default (e.g. reviewResult.qualityGate default, schemas.ts:95-101), the Sleuth Review Gate can be silently absent yet 'valid'. No test asserts the two representations agree.

gaps.title: Per-driver extraction contract divergence with no shared conformance contract
gaps.detail: codex result = file written by child (worker-driver.ts:79,97,116-139); claude result = stdout 'result' event's structured_output field, persisted by the harness (219-251); fixture = in-process object. Three different ways a result becomes 'validated state' means three independent failure surfaces and no single place that guarantees 'a valid <role>Result exists'. Adding a 4th model-agnostic driver means re-implementing extraction + getting recovery semantics right again. This works against the model-agnostic non-negotiable.

gaps.title: Codex path treats a valid artifact as success even when the process crashed (exit != 0)
gaps.detail: finalize returns ok purely from artifact validity; a non-zero/null exit becomes a 'recovery reason' annotation, not a failure (worker-driver.ts:101-111, 141-145). A child that wrote a stale or partial-but-parseable result.json from a prior turn, then crashed, can be accepted as a successful structured result. The evidence ('valid file') and the truth ('process failed') diverge — an anti-drift hazard, since acceptance later trusts that file (cli.ts:4326-4345).

gaps.title: Fixture driver bypasses validation entirely, so the harness's own tests never exercise the safeParse gate
gaps.detail: Fixture writes JSON.stringify of an in-process typed object and hardcodes structuredResultWritten:true (cli.ts:2360-2366, 2607-2618, 2079-2086). The most-used test/dev path never round-trips through parse+validate or the hand-written JSON Schema, so schema drift and extraction bugs are invisible until a real codex/claude run. There is no fixture variant that emits intentionally-malformed output to prove the block path.

recommendations.title: Generate the driver JSON Schema FROM the Zod schema (single source of truth)
recommendations.change: Replace the three hand-written writeXSchema functions (cli.ts:6460-6611) with one generator that derives JSON Schema from the Zod definitions in schemas.ts (e.g. zod-to-json-schema), keyed by role. Add a test asserting the emitted JSON Schema and the Zod schema accept/reject the same fixtures.
recommendations.rationale: Eliminates the parallel-definition drift class entirely; the schema the driver sees and the schema the harness validates against become provably the same artifact.
recommendations.missionTieIn: Evidence-vs-immutable-criteria: the contract a worker is held to must equal the contract its evidence is judged by. Removes a silent way for accepted output to miss obligations (e.g. dropped qualityGate).

recommendations.title: Add a bounded in-turn re-ask on schema failure before blocking
recommendations.change: In each role's execute path, when finalize/read reports a schema/parse failure (cli.ts:2392+2423, 2647+2663, 2117+2133), re-invoke the SAME driver session once or twice with a 'your last output failed validation: <zod error>; re-emit only the structured result' follow-up before falling through to block/escalate. Cap attempts; record each as an event.
recommendations.rationale: Captures Workflow mechanism 3's self-retry value at the harness level without changing drivers. The dominant failure (near-miss JSON) self-heals instead of stalling the slice and its dependents.
recommendations.missionTieIn: Anti-drift + verified-state throughput: stops near-misses from manufacturing 'blocked' busy-work and keeps the requirement ledger advancing on real progress.

recommendations.title: Factor extraction into a single ResultExtractor contract per driver with a shared validate/persist core
recommendations.change: Move the JSON.parse->safeParse->writeFile sequence into one shared helper that every driver's finalize calls, so drivers only supply 'where the raw result lives' (file path vs stdout structured_output field). Make 'a validated <role>Result was persisted to resultPath' the one invariant all drivers must satisfy.
recommendations.rationale: Collapses three divergent extraction surfaces into one tested code path; new model-agnostic drivers implement only raw-locating, inheriting validation, persistence, and recovery semantics.
recommendations.missionTieIn: Model-agnostic non-negotiable: makes adding codex/claude/other drivers cheap and uniform, and gives one place that guarantees the chain-of-truth link 'worker -> validated result'.

recommendations.title: Make exit-code part of the success contract and add a malformed-output fixture
recommendations.change: In codex finalize (worker-driver.ts:101-111,141-145), require exitCode===0 (or an explicit allowlisted recovery code) in addition to artifact validity, and emit a distinct 'crashed-but-artifact-present' event for operator review rather than silent ok. Add a fixture worker variant that emits invalid structured output so the block/retry path is covered by the harness's own tests.
recommendations.rationale: Closes the valid-file-overrides-crash gap and ensures the validation/block path is continuously exercised by the fast fixture path, not only by live provider runs.
recommendations.missionTieIn: 'No accepted work without evidence' and anti-drift: prevents stale/partial artifacts from a crashed process being trusted as verified state, and keeps the evidence consistent with what actually happened.

result.currentBehavior:
Recovery in agent-swarm is SESSION/RUN-level and operator-driven, not step-memoized. The pipeline is: (1) `swarm recovery scan` ages every `running` agent_run against a heartbeat staleness threshold (focus.ts findStaleAgentRuns at cli.ts:3340-3361; threshold from protocol at cli.ts:3311-3314). With `--mark-stale`/`--release` it mutates the run to `stale`/`released`, sets the affected slice to `blocked`/`closed`, raises a scoped blocker escalation (deduped by checking the run id appears in an existing active escalation, cli.ts:1526-1542), and refreshes a `recovery` checkpoint. (2) `swarm recovery revive <run-id>` resumes the SAME provider session: it requires the driver to advertise `capabilities.resume` (worker-driver.ts: codex+claude both true) and a captured `sessionId` (from the run row, else re-extracted from the run's JSONL via sessionIdFromAgentRunEvents at cli.ts:1916-1919), then spawns a NEW agentRun row (a fresh RUN id, attempt = prior-runs-for-(slice,actor)+1, cli.ts:1599) passing `resumeSessionId` so codex `exec resume <id>` / claude `--resume <id>` continues the model's own context (worker-driver.ts:69-82, 198). (3) `swarm recovery restart <run-id>` discards the session and calls executeWorkerRun with reason='restart' for a brand-new run on the same slice (cli.ts:1833-1842). On a successful revive/restart, superseded recovery escalations are cleared by substring-matching the prior run id (clearSupersededRecoveryEscalations, cli.ts:1879-1914).

Durable resume context is REGENERATED from the SQLite ledger on demand, never replayed: `swarm resume-context` (cli.ts:1342-1364) calls buildResumePacket (checkpoints.ts:43-105), which derives a role-specific markdown packet (objective, FR/AC scope, evidence status, blockers, artifact paths, doNotRedo, reviveRecommendation) purely from current store rows. Checkpoints are an upserted SNAPSHOT keyed unique(role,entity_type,entity_id) (storage.ts:188-199, 639-662) — there is exactly one row per (role,entity), overwritten each refresh, not an append-only journal. focus.ts builds richer run/slice "focus packets" (buildRunFocusPacket/buildSliceFocusPacket) and classifies failures (no_event_stream, child_idle_timeout, missing_structured_result, etc., focus.ts:477-509) to recommend revive vs restart, but these are advisory diagnostics, not memoized results.

There is NO content-addressed step-level memoization. Every dispatch unconditionally spawns the provider: `swarm run <slice>` -> executeWorkerRun(reason='direct_run') (cli.ts:828-850, 2253-) has no guard for an already-implemented/accepted slice and no prompt-hash lookup; it always writes a new prompt, inserts a new agentRun, and on success ALWAYS inserts a fresh worker_result evidence row (insertEvidence is a plain INSERT with a random EVD id, storage.ts:552-559; cli.ts:2423-2433). Re-running an identical worker/reviewer/verify unit re-does the model work and appends duplicate evidence — re-running a step is NOT idempotent in storage. Worker/reviewer results are obtained by PARSE-THEN-VALIDATE, not a forced-tool self-retry loop: drivers point the provider at an output schema file and read the resulting on-disk artifact (codex `--output-schema/--output-last-message`) or the `structured_output` field of claude's result event, then run Zod safeParse (worker-driver.ts:116-139, 219-251 against workerResultSchema, schemas.ts:38-53). On safeParse failure the run is simply marked `failed` with a failureReason; the harness itself does not auto-retry — a human/overseer decides revive or restart. IDs are random UUIDs (ids.ts:19) and every write stamps `new Date().toISOString()`, so runs are inherently non-replayable and non-deterministic at the storage layer.

result.workflowComparison: Workflow mechanism 2 (content-addressed result journal) keys every agent() call by v2:sha256(prompt+opts), stores the VALIDATED result under that key in journal.jsonl, and on resume replays unchanged steps for free, re-running only from the first changed call onward — exact, cheap, step-level memoization. agent-swarm has essentially the inverse model on the resume/idempotency axis. What it HAS that Workflow lacks: durable cross-process state in SQLite, provider-session-level resume (codex/claude session continuation, which Workflow does not do — Workflow re-runs the whole leaf), structured evidence with FR/AC linkage, and operator-grade failure triage (focus packets, failure classes). What it LACKS vs mechanism 2: (a) no step-level memoization — an identical worker/reviewer/verify unit is fully re-executed and bills the model again; (b) re-running a step is not idempotent in storage — it appends a duplicate evidence row and a new run; (c) no deterministic replay — random ids + wall-clock timestamps violate the Workflow ban on Date.now()/Math.random() in the control plane, so a "resume" can never be a free replay, only a regenerated snapshot. agent-swarm's "checkpoint/resume packet" is a state SNAPSHOT for an LLM to re-read (mechanism 5 fresh-context isolation), not a memoized RESULT cache (mechanism 2). On schema enforcement (mechanism 3) the comparison is partial: agent-swarm forces structured output via an output-schema file + Zod validation, but validation is post-hoc parse-then-validate that marks failure, NOT the tool-layer self-retry-until-valid loop Workflow uses, so the model does not auto-correct in-harness.

gaps.title: Re-running any step is non-idempotent and bills the model again
gaps.detail: executeWorkerRun (cli.ts:2253) and the reviewer/overseer dispatchers have no 'already done / unchanged inputs' check. A `swarm run <slice>` on an accepted/implemented slice, or a re-dispatch after a crash mid-pipeline, re-spawns the provider and appends a duplicate worker_result evidence row (storage.ts:552 unconditional INSERT). This directly burns budget on work that did not change verified state — the exact anti-drift the mission warns against ('resist busy work that does not move verified state').

gaps.title: No content-addressed result journal; resume cannot replay completed units for free
gaps.detail: There is no key over (role,sliceId,frAcRef,prompt,skill-binding). A multi-slice overseer run that dies after 9 of 10 slices, when restarted, has no mechanism to recognize the 9 unchanged units and skip them; only provider-session revive of a single in-flight run exists (cli.ts:1572). result.currentBehavior:
Reviewer/verifier findings flow straight through to repair dispatch and human queues with NO independent skeptic step that challenges a finding's actionability before it acts.

The pipeline is a single-pass judge -> deterministic gate -> queue, all default-ACCEPT of the finding:

1) The reviewer agent ("Sleuth Review Gate") is dispatched with a prompt (cli.ts:3717-3802) instructing it to return a structured `reviewResult` with `status` (accepted|repair_required|blocked|human_required), per-ref `frAcFindings`, a `qualityGate` (7 named dimensions, each with status/risk/finding), `requiredFixes`, `escalations`, and `recommendation`. Its result is obtained by parse-then-validate: the agent writes a JSON file which `readReviewResultFile` reads and `reviewResultSchema.safeParse`s (cli.ts:3846-3865; worker-driver.ts uses --output-schema for codex and StructuredOutput-then-write for claude, finalize at worker-driver.ts:101-106,219-245). Schema invalidity blocks but is never adversarially re-judged.

2) `applyReviewOutcome` (cli.ts:3867-3959) takes that ONE result at face value. It computes an effectiveStatus, then for EVERY escalation the reviewer emitted it calls `insertReviewEscalation` verbatim (cli.ts:3885-3887), raises an extra blocker if the quality gate produced any blocking reason (cli.ts:3888-3897 via `reviewQualityBlockingReasons`, cli.ts:4230-4243), sets slice status to `repairing` (if repair_required) or `blocked` (cli.ts:3923-3924), and records `review.blocked_acceptance` with `requiredFixes`. No second agent ever evaluates whether a finding is correct, in-scope, or worth acting on.

3) The deterministic verifier (`verify`, cli.ts:973-1004) re-reads that same review via `readLatestReviewGate` (cli.ts:4094-4164). A SINGLE non-passing finding, `stubOrHardcodeRisk === "high"`, or any quality-gate blocking reason flips the whole slice to not-passed and `repairing`/`blocked` (cli.ts:1001-1004). Pure boolean AND of gates; no skeptic, no severity/actionability filter.

4) Repair dispatch: a `repairing` slice is fed back through `buildSliceRepairContext` (cli.ts:4166-4202), whose `latestRepairReviewContext` lifts the reviewer's `requiredFixes`/`recommendation`/nonPassingRefs straight into the next worker prompt (cli.ts:6408-6414, 5443). So the unchallenged finding directly authors the repair task. The loop is bounded only by `--max-repair-attempts` (default 8; cli.ts:332,355), not by any judgement that the finding deserved action.

5) Human path (the observed `human_verification_rework` loop): when an obligation has mode human_verification_required, `buildFrAcResults` marks the ref `awaiting_human_verification` (cli.ts:4450-4458). A human records human_verified|failed|needs_rework via `recordHumanVerification` (human-actions.ts:176-334). A `failed`/`needs_rework` decision sets the slice to `repairing`/`blocked` (human-actions.ts:231) and the queue then renders a `human_verification_rework` action whose summary literally says "Continue the run so agents can repair the slice" (human-actions.ts:388-419) and feeds `latestHumanRepairFeedback` into the repair worker (cli.ts:4204-4222). A false or out-of-scope human "failed" thus drives a fresh worker repair with zero challenge; on the next cycle the ref is re-packetized to `awaiting_human_verification` again -> the repeated rework loop.

The only thing resembling adversarial filtering is the overseer's `getOverseerEscalationSuppressionReason` (cli.ts:5751-5774) which de-dupes overseer-raised blockers; it does not judge reviewer/human finding actionability and runs only on the overseer's own blocker list.
result.workflowComparison:
Workflow mechanism 7 (adversarial verify on actionability) runs a per-finding skeptic that DEFAULTS TO REJECT and must be convinced a finding is genuine AND worth acting on now; in the forensic run it killed a finding that was factually correct but pre-existing/out-of-scope, filtering true-but-not-worth-acting-on noise BEFORE it reached any work queue.

agent-swarm has the inverse posture: findings default to ACCEPT. The Sleuth Review Gate is a strong single judge, but it is the SAME agent that produces both the finding and the verdict — there is no independent challenger between "reviewer/human emitted finding" and "finding drives `repairing` + escalation + human queue." Workflow separates production of a finding from the decision to act on it; agent-swarm fuses them. Mechanism 7's skeptic is per-finding and adversarial; agent-swarm's gates (readLatestReviewGate, reviewQualityBlockingReasons) are boolean pass/fail aggregations that AMPLIFY every finding (any single non-pass blocks the whole slice) rather than triage them. Concretely, a high-risk dimension or one nonPassingRef -> full slice block + repair churn, with no equivalent of the skeptic that asked "is this in-scope and worth a fix?".

Mission fit: a skeptic gate is squarely on-mission ("independent review includes a structured Sleuth Review Gate"; "No accepted work without evidence"). The current Sleuth gate covers accept-side rigor (don't accept hollow work); it has no symmetric REJECT-side rigor (don't burn repair/human cycles on non-actionable findings). That asymmetry is the anti-drift hazard the mission warns about: "resist busy work that does not move verified state."

The overseer is NOT a "LLM-proposes-nextCommand-each-turn" agent loop, and it is NOT a fully scripted control plane either — it is a deterministic JS loop with a single-shot LLM leaf per iteration whose job is largely to re-select a command the code has already computed.

The control loop lives in the demo runner scripts, not in src/. run-live-agent-demo.mjs:229 is `for (let turn=1; turn<=maxTurns; turn++)`. Each iteration runs, in order: (a) deterministic guards — source-mutation check, max-slices/max-agent-runs/max-runtime limits (run-live-agent-demo.mjs:231-258); (b) deterministic fault handlers — handleStaleRunFault, handleSupervisedRecovery, handleContextHandoffFault, handleLowSignalFault (260-282), each of which dispatches harness commands (e.g. `recovery scan --mark-stale`) with NO LLM involved; (c) deterministic verification when a slice isReadyForDeterministicVerify (332-411), calling `swarm verify` directly and computing accept/block from gates; and only then (d) ONE call to `swarm orchestrate ... --execute` (413-424), the single LLM overseer turn. The loop, not the LLM, decides termination, verification, recovery, and limits.

Inside the harness, executeOverseerRun (cli.ts:1979-2251) is single-shot: build prompt -> run exactly one driver turn (or fixture) -> parse one OverseerDecision -> applyOverseerDecision -> optionally execute up to executeLimit bounded commands -> return. There is no inner LLM loop and no per-turn re-planning by the model.

Crucially, the deterministic code already computes the very decision the LLM is asked to make. buildOverseerStatePacket (cli.ts:4882-5080) precomputes, for each active slice, an exact `nextCommand` + `nextCommandPurpose` (cli.ts:4911-4921: ready/blocked/repairing -> `run <slice> --actor ... --driver codex`; implemented/ready_for_review -> `review <slice> ...`), plus a `nextSourcePullQueue` whose items each carry a ready-to-run `slices pull` nextCommand (cli.ts:5252), a blockedSourceQueue with prerequisiteCommands, and a focusQueue. After the model answers, validateOverseerCommand (cli.ts:6038-6109) deterministically re-derives the same legality the packet encoded — allowlisted subcommand, slice status gating (validateOverseerChildDispatch cli.ts:6174-6232: run requires ready/blocked/repairing, review requires implemented/ready_for_review + existing worker_result evidence + no running child), pull dependency satisfaction (validateSlicesPullDependencies cli.ts:6135-6150), no shell operators — and blocks anything off-script. result.workflowComparison: Workflow mechanism 1 says the control plane is deterministic JS (loops/parallel/pipeline) and the LLM only fills leaves; agent-swarm already realizes the SPIRIT of this: the turn loop, fault recovery, verification, and limits are deterministic JS, and the overseer is a single-shot leaf. But there are three divergences. (1) The "leaf" is over-scoped: the code precomputes the exact nextCommand and then asks an LLM to pick it from a queue, then re-validates it — so an LLM round-trip is spent re-deriving a deterministic answer. Workflow would either make that selection plain code OR give the LLM a genuinely underdetermined judgement (which command, which lane, when to block) rather than an echo task. (2) The deterministic control plane lives in demo .mjs scripts, not in a reusable src/ orchestrator — so the "code control plane" is per-scenario and duplicated (run-live-agent-demo.mjs vs run-support-triage-live-demo.mjs share the same loop shape). Workflow's value is one deterministic engine with swappable leaves. (3) Workflow bans Date.now()/Math.random() to keep runs replayable and pairs the loop with a content-addressed result journal (mechanism 2) so unchanged steps replay for free; agent-swarm has neither — it uses wall-clock time throughout the loop and relies on checkpoints/resume-packets for recovery rather than step-level memoized replay. So agent-swarm matches mechanism 3 (schema-enforced leaves) strongly, matches mechanism 1 partially (deterministic loop, but LLM leaf is an echo and the engine is script-bound), and does not implement mechanism 2 at all.
